guidance: Parsing and comparison only: it says whether a version string satisfies a specifier set. It does not resolve packages, read an index, or decide what pip would install.
method: A PEP 440 version is an optional epoch, a release, and optional pre-release, post-release, dev-release and local segments: [N!]N(.N)*[{a|b|rc}N][.postN][.devN][+local]. It is normalized before anything is compared: a leading v and the -_ . separators are dropped, alpha, beta, c, pre and preview become a, b, rc, a hyphen and a number become .postN, numbers lose leading zeros and local segments are lowercased. Two versions are ordered by epoch as a whole number, then by release with the shorter one padded with zeros, then by pre-release (a dev-only release sorts below a0, a final release above rcN), post-release, dev release, and finally the local label: numeric segments compare numerically and sort above text, and a prefix sorts below its extension. Each clause applies that order. ~=X.Y.Z means >=X.Y.Z and ==X.Y.*, dropping the last release number and keeping the epoch. == and != compare releases with zero padding and ignore the candidate's local label unless the clause names one, while a .* suffix matches the epoch and release prefix. <= and >= ignore the candidate's local label; < and > refuse the boundary version itself and also a pre-release, post-release or local build of it; === compares the normalized version string literally. A pre-release candidate fails the whole set unless some clause names a pre-release, which is the PEP 440 default that pip can override. A wildcard may only follow an epoch and release numbers, <, <=, > and >= take no local label, and ~= needs at least two release numbers; those forms are refused with a message rather than guessed. The check is implemented in the browser from the published grammar and never consults pip or an index; nothing is sent, stored or uploaded.
